# 2011B Question 10 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the effects of resonance and damping on an invasive arterial blood pressure tracing.
:::

Also asked in: [2007A Question 15](/content/exams/anzca/2007/A/15/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2013B Question 8](/content/exams/anzca/2013/B/8/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} resonance and damping before linking each to waveform distortion and measured pressures. Use labelled tracings to show the differences.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Measurement System and Natural Frequency

### Resonance

### Damping Coefficient

### Underdamped, Overdamped and Optimally Damped Tracings
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**42%** of candidates passed this question.

Basic material required to pass:

Description of the measurement system was useful only if related to the following discussion

Definition of resonance and damping

Explanation of their importance and their effect on the timely measurement of the components of the blood pressure (systolic pressure, diastolic pressure, mean pressure)

Advanced material:

Quantification of the effects

Common errors/omissions/unnecessary inclusions:

Equations without definition of symbols

Input frequency is not 0 – 40Hz!

Natural resonant frequency is a property of the measuring system

Details of transduction were not required

“directionless relationships”; in a connected universe, everything influences everything else. To be of use, a relationship should include a direction of the effect, and a qualitative/quantitative indicator of the importance/magnitude

Organisational errors:

Planning in the margins or on the back of the cover is a waste of time (headings can be used in the answer)

Long lists of definitions before any factual content is a poor use of time (definitions should be embedded within the answer itself)
:::
